claims.claim: First story is The Purloined Letter; Dupin and the narrator are visited by the police Prefect G——
claims.evidence: Contents lists THE PURLOINED LETTER first; 'our old acquaintance, Monsieur G——, the Prefect of the Parisian police'
Contents lists 22 titles before 'Notes to the Second Volume'

claims.claim: In The Purloined Letter Dupin recovers a stolen letter from Minister D——
claims.evidence: 'The thief is the Minister D——'; Dupin's substituted 'fac-simile' of the letter

claims.claim: The Fall of the House of Usher ends with the house collapsing
claims.evidence: 'the deep and dank tarn at my feet closed sullenly and silently over the fragments of the "House of Usher."'

claims.claim: The Black Cat's narrator murders his wife and walls her up with the cat, whose cry betrays him
claims.evidence: 'buried the axe in her brain'; 'I had walled the monster up within the tomb!'; the cry 'consigned me to the hangman'

claims.claim: M. Valdemar is mesmerized at the point of death and held there for months
claims.evidence: 'mesmerized in articulo mortis'; 'an interval of nearly seven months'

claims.claim: In The Masque of the Red Death a masked figure of plague enters Prince Prospero's ball and all die
claims.evidence: 'a masked figure'; Prince Prospero 'fell prostrate in death'; 'one by one dropped the revellers... and died'

claims.claim: In The Cask of Amontillado Montresor lures and walls up Fortunato
claims.evidence: 'I began vigorously to wall up the entrance of the niche'

claims.claim: The Pit and the Pendulum tortures an Inquisition prisoner
claims.evidence: 'the dungeons of the Inquisition'; Toledo; the pendulum

claims.claim: William Wilson is haunted by a double
claims.evidence: 'my namesake'; 'The same name! the same contour of person!'

claims.claim: The Tell-Tale Heart's killer, hearing the dead man's heart, confesses
claims.evidence: 'It was the beating of the old man's heart'; the killer is driven to tear up the planks before the officers

claims.claim: Roderick Usher, last of his house, with his sister Madeline
claims.evidence: 'the last of the ancient race of the Ushers'; 'the lady Madeline'

claims.claim: Dupin a Paris detective; Prospero a ruler; Montresor and Fortunato murderer and victim; Wilson pursued by his double
claims.evidence: Dupin at Paris consulted by the Prefect of police; 'Prince Prospero'; walling-up scene; namesake passages
